Q: Image doesn't exist, but it does A:

The way I catch _tkinter errors is by using str and compare it against the one I want to catch. So every other error will be raised and only the specific error will be handled

For example:

except tk.TclError as e:
            if str(e) == ("can't invoke "
                          '"tk" command: '
                          'application has been destroyed'):

In your case it should look like:

msg = str(e)
if msg[0:25] == "_tkinter.TclError: image " and msg[-13:] == "doesn't exist":
    continue
else:
    raise e

Q: WebRTC working on Chrome/Edge and Safari but does not works on Firefox or opera A:

This is a known Firefox behavior on localhost, especially with WebRTC.

Firefox applies stricter security rules than Chrome. On http://localhost, features like getUserMedia, autoplay, and WebRTC may fail or behave differently. Common issues include requiring a user interaction, stricter codec/SDP validation, and different handling of media permissions.

Recommended solutions:

Use https even for local testing, or try http://127.0.0.1 instead of localhost

Ensure media playback starts from a user gesture

Avoid hard-coding codecs or SDP (Firefox is less tolerant)

Test on a real HTTPS domain early

This is a browser limitation, not an implementation bug.

Q: Situations where R strips attributes for S3 classes, and how to work around or avoid them? A:

The thing is: you have a wrong assumption/expectation/mental model of how a ifelse should function on structures.

If you do

C <- ifelse(c(F,F,T),A,B)

it is iterating through A and B structures' first arguments only, the txt_pvals and not through the entire structure.

This is also what you see:

> C
[1] "1.5e-90"  "2.1e-230" "1.9e-250"

It is the txt_pval vector newly generated using the vectorized ifelse. So meta informations (attributes) stay out of the calculation by definition - the structs themselves are ignored, if you apply ifelse.

If you want a the end of the calculation a tinypval structure instead, then make one!

A <- make_tinypval(c('4e-40','3.6e-150','1.9e-250'))
B <- make_tinypval(c('1.5e-90','2.1e-230','9.5e-60'))
C <- make_tinypval(ifelse(c(F,F,T),A,B))

> C
[1] "1.5e-90"  "2.1e-230" "1.9e-250"
attr(,"log10p")
[1]  -89.82391 -229.67778 -249.72125
attr(,"class")
[1] "tinypval"

So what you actually want is a constructor function which can generate out of a logical vector and two tinypval structures a new tinypval structure.

You can abstract it into a new function:

combine_to_tinypval <- function(selector, tinypval1, tinypval2) 
  make_tinypval(ifelse(selector, tinypval1, tinypval2))
## if the function body is only 1 expression, you can leave out
## the { }.

# which you apply then:
C <- combine_to_tinypval(c(F,F,T), A, B)

C
## returning:
[1] "1.5e-90"  "2.1e-230" "1.9e-250"
attr(,"log10p")
[1]  -89.82391 -229.67778 -249.72125
attr(,"class")
[1] "tinypval"
